description:
Jurassic Park Series 1 Stegosaurus figure, released by Kenner in 1993. This figure was part of the original wave of toys based on the blockbuster "Jurassic Park" movie. The Stegosaurus figure is notable for its "Dino-Damage" wound feature, which allowed a piece of its flesh to be removed, revealing a wound beneath—a common feature among the toys in this line to simulate injuries. Additionally, it features a "Whip-Action Spiked Tail," where pulling the tail back would cause it to spring forward, mimicking the tail's defensive action.

This Stegosaurus toy stands approximately 7 inches tall and was designed to be suitable for children aged 4 and up. It was released with a unique UPC code of 0 76281 61014 6, making it identifiable among collectors and enthusiasts​ (Dino Toy Blog)​​ (Shop OB Toys)​​ (Figure Realm)​.

description:
Giganotosaurus is a genus of large theropod dinosaur that lived in what is now Argentina, during the early Cenomanian age of the Late Cretaceous period, approximately 99.6 to 95 million years ago. The holotype specimen was discovered in the Candeleros Formation of Patagonia in 1993 and is almost 70% complete. The animal was named Giganotosaurus carolinii in 1995; the genus name translates to "giant southern lizard", and the specific name honors the discoverer, Ruben Carolini. A dentary bone, a tooth, and some tracks, discovered before the holotype, were later assigned to this animal. The genus attracted much interest and became part of a scientific debate about the maximum sizes of theropod dinosaurs.

name: Etruscan seal (right navicular)
description:
3D scan of the right navicular of the Etruscan seal (*Pliophoca etrusca*).

The fossil skeleton of *Pliophoca etrusca*, collected in1900 by Antonio di Paco from the upper Pliocene (Piacenzian) clays of Casa Nuova locality, near Orciano Pisano (Tuscany, Pisa province, Italy) is the best preserved and most complete fossil seal of the northern hemysphere and holotype of the fossil species *Pliophoca etrusca*.
This specimen was first described in detail and referred to the extant Mediterranean monk seal *Monachus albiventer* (=*Monachus monachus*) by Ugolini (1902); later on Tavani (1941) redescribed this specimen and assigned it to the new genus and species of monachine seals *Pliophoca etrusca*. It was finally redescribed by Berta et al. (2015).

Specimen: *Pliophoca etrusca* Tavani, 1941

name: Fossil brown bear (first phalanx)
description:
3D scan of the first phalanx of a fossil brown bear (*Ursus arctos*). 


Fossil of a prime adult female skull of brown bear. The specimen was found in "Abisso Oriano Coltelli" cave (44°05'35,0 N, 10°14'47,0" E, labelled T/Lu 642 in the Tuscan register of caves) which opens at 1209 m a.s.l on the western slope of "Monte Alto di Sella" (Apuan Alps). The mammal assemblage collected consists of 486 investigated specimens, 127 of which belong to an individual skeleton of brown bear. The bear died from non-violent causes, probably during hibernation. The specimen was dated providing a conventional age of 6480 ± 40 14 C ka BP (Holocene).
More information : https://amq.aiqua.it/index.php/amq/article/view/112
